body: Original reference implementation of "3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering"
plain_description: Transform ordinary photographs into photorealistic 3D scenes you can explore in real time — no expensive 3D modeling or manual work required. The technology renders immersive walkthroughs at 30+ frames per second on standard GPU hardware, making high-quality 3D capture practical for the first time. Originally a research breakthrough, it is now the foundation for a wave of new 3D visualization and digital twin products.
technical_description: The official PyTorch reference implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting for real-time novel-view synthesis. The system accepts multi-view image sets, runs COLMAP for Structure-from-Motion camera calibration, and optimizes a scene as a set of anisotropic 3D Gaussians with interleaved densification and adaptive density control. Training requires a CUDA-capable NVIDIA GPU (Compute Capability 7.0+) with ~24 GB VRAM for reference quality and uses a custom CUDA rasterizer for differentiable rendering. The trained representation renders at ≥30 fps at 1080p resolution via the SIBR OpenGL-based real-time viewer. The codebase includes the PyTorch optimizer, a network viewer for training monitoring, a standalone real-time viewer, and a COLMAP-based image-to-dataset conversion pipeline. Optional features: accelerated fused rasterizer (>2× training speedup), monocular depth regularization, per-image exposure compensation, and EWA anti-aliasing filtering.
title: 3D Gaussian Splatting
